chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: Jack Johnson's nightclub in the Dunbar
summary: Jack Johnson opened a floor-show club in the Dunbar's dining room in 1933, unprofitable.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You also mentioned before when we were talking about the Dunbar, that there was someplace downstairs that had music. Was it a lounge or something?

In the Dunbar, at one time, there was a nightclub there. It was in what was originally the main dining room. But this nightclub was opened in 1933 by the old world's heavyweight champion, Jack Johnson, and he ran it for about a year or so and called it Jack Johnson's.
Was it, what? A regular floor show?^ type entertainment?
Yes, he had a floor show. That's what it was.
And after a year,^ did it just cease to be? (inaudible).
It was never really a paying proposition. It didn't go over as big as they thought it was.
Late, like in the '40s, there was a small bar with on a trio.
That was just a bar, just --
Didn't Gerry Wiggins used to work in there?
I don't know. It was a small-time --
But in between going on musically?
It was a small operation, no.
